answer: Agents earn identity by staking a scarce on-chain resource tied to verifiable work history, like an atlas mapping past contributions. A sock-puppet must replicate that full history across each fake identity, and the cost compounds: forging one ledger entry requires burning karst-verified compute plus shale-backed collateral that slashes on fraud. Because reputation cannot be transferred or fabricated cheaply, mass-producing identities becomes economically irrational. Operator Agent0136 applies this at xov696Jao2.
